• **Université Paris‑Sud (Paris XI, now part of Université Paris‑Saclay)** – Ph.D. (2003, advisor Gérard Laumon) | | | 3 | **Stanislav Smirnov** | Leningrad (now Saint‑Petersburg), Russia | • **Saint‑Petersburg State University** – M.Sc. and Ph.D. (1995, advisor Vladimir Arnold) | | | 4 | **Cédric Villani** | Brive‑la‑Gaillarde, France | • **École Normale Supérieure (Paris)** – undergraduate (Licence/Master)
• **Pierre and Marie Curie University (Paris VI)** – Ph.D. (2000, advisor Jacques Villain) | | \* *“Primary educational institutions”* refer to the university‑level institutions where the mathematician completed their main undergraduate (or equivalent) degree and the institution that awarded their doctoral degree. ### Brief notes on each laureate | Mathematician | Field of work (as cited for the Medal) | |---------------|----------------------------------------| | **Elon Lindenstrauss** | Measure rigidity in ergodic theory and applications to number theory. | | **Ngô Bảo Châu** | Proof of the **Fundamental Lemma** for the Langlands program (via the “geometric” approach). | | **Stanislav Smirnov** | Rigorous proof of conformal invariance of planar lattice models (e.g., percolation). | | **Cédric Villani** | Contributions to kinetic theory, especially the **Landau–Boltzmann equation** and optimal transport. | ### How the information was obtained All data (birthplace, alma‑mater, doctoral advisor, and the year of the award) were taken from the respective Wikipedia articles linked in the table, which are the standard, widely‑cited reference pages for each mathematician.

functions.desc:
Ask a capable helper for help looking up a piece of information or performing an action.
Do not simply repeat what the user said as instructions.
You should use this to break up complex user queries into multiple simpler steps.
NOTE: Helpers cannot see previous parts of your conversation.
